solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Annoyed about one insect in pastry

indicators.note: the annoyed word goes about, that is around, the numeral one

parts.note: annoyed means cross
one is the Roman numeral I
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered baker discovers a bug baked into a pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Annoyed' looks like the baker's mood but just supplies the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A croissant is a crescent-shaped roll of flaky, buttery pastry.

clue.text: What has origins in Celtic rural Wales, traditionally heard?

definitions.text: What has origins in Celtic rural Wales, traditionally heard?

indicators.note: origins in means the first letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: A question about something rooted in rural Welsh tradition and listened to.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials spell the word, and the whole clue also describes it: a traditional Welsh instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The crwth is an ancient bowed lyre played in Wales, a Celtic musical instrument heard at traditional gatherings.

clue.text: Flowering potatoes, say, to appear out of the earth

definitions.text: to appear out of the earth

parts.note: plants that are out are in flower
potatoes are an example of a crop

explanation.surface: Potato plants in bloom begin to show above the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, rock outcrops when it protrudes through the soil at the surface.

clue.text: Brilliant author in academic setting I dismissed

indicators.note: the academic word is the setting in which the author is placed
dismissed means the letter I is removed

parts.note: academic means studious
pen is a rare old word for an author

explanation.surface: A dazzling writer in a university, from which the speaker has been sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissed' removes I, leaving STUDOUS; 'setting' puts the author inside. Pen for an author is a rare old usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupendous means astonishingly great or impressive, close to brilliant.

clue.text: Ancient cave to which enchantress is reduced

indicators.note: reduced means trimmed at both ends, leaving letters from within the word

explanation.surface: A sorceress banished to live in an old cave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is reduced' trims ENCH and SS off enchantress.
explanation.definitionFit: Antre is an archaic, poetic word for a cavern, used by Shakespeare in Othello.

clue.text: Attempt to imprison every queen could be this

definitions.text: Attempt to imprison every queen could be this

indicators.note: imprison means the attempt word encloses the others

parts.note: an attempt is a try
every means each
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the regular abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: A plot to lock up the monarch would count as betrayal.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: imprisoning a queen would be treason against the crown.
explanation.definitionFit: Plotting to jail a monarch is betrayal of the crown, so treachery or treason.

clue.text: Abandon urge to follow Democrat

indicators.note: the urge word comes to follow, so it is written after, the Democrat letter

parts.note: D is the usual abbreviation for a Democrat in US politics
an itch is a restless urge or longing

explanation.surface: A voter feels an urge to desert the Democrats and follow someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to follow' puts ITCH after D.
explanation.definitionFit: To ditch something is the informal way of saying you abandon or discard it.

clue.text: Where one will find Qataris party hard: answer _____

parts.note: a do is a party
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A fill-in-the-blank quiz: where do Qataris party hard?
explanation.definitionFit: Doha is the capital city of Qatar, home to many Qataris.

clue.text: Cover provided by EU and NATO repositioning around November

indicators.note: the repositioned letters go around the November letter
repositioning means the letters of EU and NATO are shifted into a new order

parts.note: N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Military protection offered by the European Union and NATO repositioning troops in November.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repositioning' turns EUNATO into TONEAU, and N goes 'around' into the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonneau cover is a fitted protective sheet over the open back of a pickup or open car.

clue.text: Welcome little new for traditional occasion

parts.note: hallo is a greeting of welcome
wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: Welcoming a small newcomer is a time-honoured custom.
explanation.definitionFit: Halloween, 31 October, is a traditional festival with costumes and trick-or-treating.

clue.text: Be uncomfortably hot over getting quite stripped down in this?

definitions.text: Be uncomfortably hot over getting quite stripped down in this?

indicators.note: over in a down-reading sense of turned over: the word for being uncomfortably hot is written backwards

parts.note: to stew is to be uncomfortably hot, as in a stuffy room

indicators.note: stripped down means the outer letters of the following word are removed, leaving its middle

explanation.surface: A diver complains of overheating before peeling most of the way out of the rubber suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns STEW into WETS; 'stripped down' takes Q and E off QUITE, leaving UIT. The whole clue also describes the garment: you can bake in one and then peel it off.
explanation.definitionFit: A wetsuit is the close-fitting rubber garment worn by divers and surfers, notoriously hot and hard to peel off.

clue.text: Fuel putting out no heat and just the first hint of light

indicators.note: putting out here means disturbing or displacing, so the letters of no heat are rearranged
only the first letter, the slightest hint, of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: Instructions for a fuel that gives no heat, only a faint glimmer of light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting out' rearranges NOHEAT into ETHANO; 'just the first hint of' gives L from light.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethanol, the alcohol in drinks, is also burned as a motor and lamp fuel, often blended with petrol.

clue.text: Parasite given heroin by old doctor

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin
leech is an old word for a physician, from the days of bloodletting

explanation.surface: A sponger is slipped heroin by a disgraced former physician.
explanation.definitionFit: The horse leech is a large blood-sucking worm, and by extension any insatiable hanger-on or parasite.

clue.text: Lead killing the last pair of river birds

indicators.note: killing removes the final two letters of the bird word

parts.note: herons are wading birds of rivers and marshes

explanation.surface: A shooter takes aim with lead at two river birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'killing the last pair of' drops NS from HERONS. 'Lead' is not the metal of shot but the leading role.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero is the lead, the principal male role in a play or film.

clue.text: Sweet to shoot big cat for current king in Zaire

indicators.note: one thing for another means swapping it in, so the shooting phrase takes the place of current and king

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
R, from Rex, is the abbreviation for king
to bag game is to shoot it
a lion is a big cat

explanation.surface: A colonial hunting party bags a lion in Zaire.
explanation.walkthrough: In ZAIRE, the letters IR are replaced by BAGLION.
explanation.definitionFit: Zabaglione is an Italian dessert of whipped egg yolks, sugar and Marsala, a sweet in British usage.

clue.text: Fast hit I had wanted

parts.note: to rap is to hit sharply
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A boxer wanted to land a quick punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanted' is only a link: the two pieces are what is wanted to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid is a direct synonym of quick or swift, as in a fast or rapid pace.

clue.text: America, say, abolishing cents quietly to put out another version

indicators.note: abolishing means the cents letter is removed from the country word

parts.note: the United States is an example of a republic
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: The United States quietly scraps the cent coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abolishing' takes C out of REPUBLIC.
explanation.definitionFit: To republish is to issue a book or text again, often in a new edition.

clue.text: Previous erratum to be corrected in returned English page

indicators.note: the corrected erratum sits in, that is inside, the returned pair
returned means the English and page letters are read backwards
an erratum to be corrected is to be put right, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An earlier misprint must be fixed on an English page sent back to the printer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns EP into PE; 'to be corrected' gives REMATUR, which sits 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Premature means too early, so here previous in the sense of hasty or acting before the right time.

clue.text: One's rapt afresh with saint and angel

indicators.note: afresh means the letters are put together anew in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone is enraptured once more, alongside a saint and an angel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afresh' rearranges ONESRAPT into PATRONES, and S is added. 'angel' is not heavenly here.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel is a backer who funds a theatre production; a woman doing so is a patroness.

clue.text: Pull up an oak, perhaps, reportedly for wooden flooring

indicators.note: reportedly means the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: to pull up a car is to park it; an oak is an example of a tree, giving a tree

explanation.surface: A forester is told to pull up an oak to make a wooden floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull up' is stopping a car, not uprooting.
explanation.definitionFit: Parquetry is a floor of small wooden blocks laid in a geometric pattern such as herringbone.

clue.text: Clean what could be venerated mosaic cross here with due care

parts.note: to rub is to polish or clean
an icon is a holy image, venerated, which may be a mosaic

explanation.surface: Instructions for cleaning a holy mosaic and crossing oneself carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like the sign of the cross; it means crossing a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar crossed the Rubicon in 49 BC, so crossing it is an irrevocable step to take with care.

clue.text: Old ship with nitrogen gas

parts.note: the Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek myth
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: An ancient vessel carries a cargo of nitrogen gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Argon is an inert noble gas, used for example in light bulbs.

clue.text: Scowl in dreadful shot

parts.note: grim means dreadful
an ace is an unreturnable serve, a winning shot in tennis

explanation.surface: A tennis player frowns after a terrible shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A grimace is a twisted facial expression of disgust or pain, like a scowl.

clue.text: Infant born during recess

indicators.note: during means the born letter comes within the recess word

parts.note: a bay is a recess, as in a bay window
B is the abbreviation for born, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A child is born while Parliament is in recess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recess' looks like a holiday but is an alcove or bay.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby is an infant, a very young child.

clue.text: Offensive when company replaces one for seeking advice

indicators.note: company replaces one means the company letters go where the one letter was

parts.note: offensive means insulting
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A rude remark made when a firm takes over from a single person giving guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: In INSULTING, the first I becomes CO.
explanation.definitionFit: Consulting someone means going to them for their advice or expert opinion.

clue.text: Parking under high cliff and steep bank

indicators.note: in a down clue, under puts the parking letter below, so after, the cliff word

parts.note: a scar is a steep rocky cliff

explanation.surface: A car parked beneath a towering cliff and a steep slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarp is a steep slope or escarpment.

clue.text: Magnificence of head of grey parrot

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the word grey

parts.note: a lory is a brightly coloured parrot

explanation.surface: Admiring the splendid grey head of a parrot.
explanation.definitionFit: Glory is splendour or magnificence.

clue.text: Small-scale revolt ousting character in Athens

indicators.note: ousting means the Greek letter is thrown out of the revolt word

parts.note: a mutiny is a revolt
mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A minor uprising in Athens topples a public figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' is a letter, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny means very small, so small-scale.

clue.text: Under control around cold ski slope?

indicators.note: the under-control phrase goes around the cold letter

parts.note: in line means under control, behaving properly
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A skier keeps things under control on a chilly slope.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a ski slope is just one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An incline is any slope or gradient, and a ski run is one kind of incline.

clue.text: In central Java, Jock saw odd box tree

indicators.note: central means only the middle letters of each word that follows are taken

explanation.surface: On holiday in Java, a Scotsman spots a strange box tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central' covers all five words: AV, OC, A, D, O. Box is a real tree, which makes 'box tree' a tempting false definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocado is the tropical American tree that bears the avocado pear.

clue.text: Practical arrangement of Haydn

indicators.note: an arrangement of a piece of music suggests the composer's name is rearranged

explanation.surface: A practical arrangement of a Haydn piece for a smaller band.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone handy is good with their hands and practically skilled.

clue.text: Utterly like a road being repaired by engineers inside arch

indicators.note: the road and engineers pieces go inside the arch word

parts.note: arch means sly or knowing, as in an arch smile
a road being repaired is said to be up, as in road up
REME, the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, is a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A road under repair by engineers beneath a bridge arch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arch' is an adjective, not a bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Supremely means to the highest degree, so completely or utterly.
